spec_issues: The reviewer rubric names the held-out source, the SVGenius text-to-SVG benchmark, but the agents are not told it (tests/task/review.py:21-24). CONTRACT.md:3 only says 'don't train on any public text-to-SVG evaluation suite'. Several agents saw xiaoooobai/SVGenius or OmniSVG/MMSVGBench in Hugging Face search listings (Fable 5uus6j, DeepSeek 3r8r1s, Argon 5tnbkq [104]). None downloaded them, so the gap did no harm here.

The 30 public examples are all in the 'simple' stratum. The held-out set of 254 is macro-averaged over complexity groups (CONTRACT.md:11; the self-check warns that 'The public examples are simple icons only'). The 30 public examples are therefore a poor guide to the score. Agents that relied only on them (Muse 4nyu6t, Muse 32wvxy) fell below the floor.

Training on the provided examples and selecting with them are explicitly allowed (prompt; review.py:25-26). Distillation from teacher models through Spin OpenRouter is allowed (review.py:18). Scaling lm_head and averaging the session's own adapters are allowed (review.py:15-17). Opus i9hng5 scaled lm_head by 0.625 'which mathematically mimics T=0.8 sampling while reporting as T=0.5' [158]. That is within the rule.
verifier_issues: Score = (raw - 0.1885) / (0.7535 - 0.1885), clamped to [0, 1] (tests/task/task.yaml:93). The floor is untouched gpt-oss-20b at temperature 0.5. It is the mean of two runs, 0.1955 and 0.1815 (task.yaml:95-98), so the floor itself moves by about 0.014 raw, or 2.5 points. The contract adds that 'grading the same weights twice can differ by about 0.01 in the raw score'.

8 of 18 trials have raw scores below the floor and score exactly 0 (raw 0.041 to 0.173). The clamp hides how much worse than the base model they are. Four more trials sit within one floor-noise band of 0: Fable 5uus6j 0.2038, Argon 5tnbkq 0.2036, Fable 23ajzb 0.1996 and DeepSeek 3r8r1s 0.1995. Their scores of 1.9 to 2.7 are not distinguishable from 'no gain'.

The judge (gpt-6-sol) can be called through the agents' own Spin OpenRouter key. Several trials used it to filter teacher samples or pick checkpoints: Fable 4vubq5 [35] 'best-of-2 selection by the gpt-6-sol judge'; Opus 2y9b1x and 6b1uc5 filter on rubric grades; DeepSeek kei48h [505] 'The actual judge model openai/gpt-6-sol IS available'. Nothing forbids it, but those trials optimised directly against the grader's own model.

A Spin OpenRouter outage on 2026-10-21 ('All models return 409', DeepSeek kei48h [537]; 24zhyt's closing message: 'The gpt-6-sol judge proxy was down at submission time') stopped both DeepSeek trials judging their final models. Both were already far below the floor on their own measurements, so the outage did not change their scores.
task_level.noise: Wallets order sensibly for Opus (0, 5.2, 18.0) and Astra (0, 8.3, 14.0). Fable is non-monotone (2.7, 2.0, 20.3), but its $10 and $50 trials are both within floor noise. Argon (0, 2.7, 0), Muse (0, 0, 0) and DeepSeek (1.9, 0, 0) never clearly beat the base model. With about 1.8 points of grading noise and 2.5 points of floor noise, the $10 'winner' (Fable 2.7 vs DeepSeek 1.9) is a coin flip, and the $200 order (Fable 20.3 vs Opus 18.0) is about one noise unit apart. Only the $50 margin (Astra 8.3 vs Opus 5.2) and the separation of the $200 top three from the rest are robust.
task_level.elicitation: Muse underspent badly. It used $36 of $200 in 4.2 h (4nyu6t) and $21 of $50 (j6w17x), with weak teachers (gemini-2.5-flash) or public icon corpora, and submitted below the floor. DeepSeek (Claude Code, max effort) spent little on GPUs and SFT'd on large public icon corpora (svgen-500k, Iconify, svg-stack), which degraded the model (3r8r1s found 'A full SFT on svg-stack ... collapses the model'). Astra's harness offers multi-agent tools. 5yr6t0 used wait/subagent calls (25), but nothing irregular came of it. Argon trajectories are not in chronological step order (5f60ys steps 1-1635 interleave two sessions; the submit is at step [1057], 02:28 UTC, after the last-numbered step [1635] at 00:44). The DeepSeek reviews were skipped by the operator. I reviewed all three: no rule violations.
task_level.epoch_rationale: No false positive, false negative or infrastructure zero was found. All 8 zeros are honest below-floor results, and the reviewer's three passes and the three DeepSeek skips all hold up. The $10 winner (Fable 2.7 vs DeepSeek 1.9) and the $200 winner (Fable 20.3 vs Opus 18.0) are within the scorer's own noise, but that is noise, not a scoring defect.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: No gaming. Every positive score came from distilling a frontier teacher (mostly gpt-6-luna) into LoRA adapters on synthetic instructions spread over complexity tiers, then merging and averaging. The decisive factors were teacher quality, enough data, and fixing failure modes (over-long or unterminated SVGs, schema violations). Two ideas were small and task-specific: Fable 23ajzb numbered top-level element ids so the model could count elements and stop, and Astra 5pavh1 put part labels and a completion marker in SVG comments. The best result reached only 20% of the way from the base model to the references.
